item.title: Parcheo virtual vs. parcheo: cuándo proteger una API en lugar de redesplegarla
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source. (Clean-up failed for this item, so the body is a truncated excerpt of the original.)

El parcheo virtual bloquea temporalmente una vía conocida para llegar a un fallo de software mientras el código vulnerable sigue en su sitio. Úsalo cuando puedas cubrir el tráfico de API afectado antes de lo que tardarías en desplegar una corrección de forma segura. Aplica el parche y verifica la flota afectada en cuanto la compilación corregida esté lista.

El 23 de noviembre de 2026, OpenAI y Cisco presentaron Shirudo, un proyecto Linux de código abierto que puede cargar protecciones eBPF específicas en un sistema en ejecución. Pone el foco en una decisión habitual para el equipo de guardia. Si la corrección permanente tarda horas en validarse, ¿puedes reducir la exposición ahora sin romper las solicitudes de las que dependen tus clientes? Anuncio de Shirudo de OpenAI

Parcheo virtual frente a parcheo convencional

Un parche virtual es un control compensatorio. Tu inventario sigue mostrando la versión vulnerable mientras el control está activo. Mantén abierto el ticket de remediación y registra allí la regla, el propietario y la fecha de retirada prevista. Guía de parcheo virtual de OWASP

Un parche convencional puede ser una biblioteca actualizada en una imagen de contenedor o una compilación corregida de tu propio servicio. Haz seguimiento de lo que realmente se está ejecutando en la flota. Una imagen corregida en el registro dice poco sobre los workers antiguos que siguen atendiendo solicitudes. Guía de gestión de parches empresariales de NIST

¿Cuándo conviene usar un escudo para una API?

Usa un escudo cuando se cumplan tres condiciones.

- El control cubre el tráfico afectado. Confirma qué rutas de entrada y cargas de trabajo están dentro del alcance, incluidos los llamadores internos y el procesamiento en segundo plano cuando corresponda.

- Puedes validarlo antes que la compilación corregida. Usa tráfico representativo de staging para comprobar el comportamiento previsto de la regla y confirmar que las solicitudes normales siguen funcionando.

- Alguien es responsable de la salida. Asigna el despliegue del parche, acuerda la evidencia de cobertura y fija una fecha de revisión para el cambio temporal.

Supongamos que una API de objetos tiene una función opcional de procesamiento vulnerable y que el gateway ya admite desactivar el acceso a esa función. Tu equipo puede evaluar rápidamente el comportamiento con esa función desactivada mientras vuelve a compilar y probar el servicio. Las lecturas de colección y de detalle deberían seguir funcionando. Si los clientes usan la función opcional, informa a soporte de qué respuesta recibirán esos clientes y cuánto tiempo es probable que dure el cambio.

Mide ambos lados del equilibrio. Compara el tiempo previsto para aplicar la regla con el tiempo necesario para llevar una compilación corregida al mismo conjunto de cargas de trabajo. Durante el despliegue, vigila el éxito de las solicitudes normales, la latencia y los recuentos de rechazos. Un aumento de los rechazos necesita contexto. Puede ser que el control esté haciendo su trabajo o que se trate de un flujo de trabajo de cliente que tus datos de prueba de staging no contemplaron.

Prioriza un parche inmediato cuando la compilación corregida esté lista, un despliegue canario tenga buen estado y el despliegue llegue a las instancias expuestas con la misma rapidez que la regla temporal. Si ningún control fiable cubre la ruta afectada y el riesgo justifica una actuación inmediata, considera restringir el acceso o desactivar la capacidad afectada mientras se prepara la corrección. Si tienes evidencia de compromiso, inicia la respuesta a incidentes junto con la remediación.

¿Dónde debe ejecutarse un escudo de API?

Elige el punto de aplicación según lo que pueda observar y qué solicitudes deben pasar por él. Un firewall de aplicaciones web (WAF) en un gateway de API evalúa allí el tráfico HTTP. Un escudo de tiempo de ejecución de Linux aplica la política donde el host puede observar la actividad relevante. Cada uno depende de la cobertura en su propia capa.

Una regla de gateway encaja en un cambio expuesto por HTTP cuando el gateway ve los atributos de solicitud relevantes y todas las solicitudes afectadas pasan por él. Verifica el alcance con el inventario de servicios. Si un servicio gestiona trabajo de varias fuentes, incluye esas rutas en tu plan de remediación. Para ver un ejemplo específico de dependencia sobre por qué importa el inventario de componentes, consulta nuestra cobertura de una vulnerabilidad de Node.js Brotli.

Un control en el host tiene sentido cuando el comportamiento relevante es visible en el host y puedes establecer cobertura en los kernels y las cargas de trabajo afectados. Su ubicación puede acercar el control al componente que proteges, con sus propios requisitos de despliegue y reversión. Mantén las comprobaciones de autorización de la aplicación en el plan de pruebas de lanzamiento. Un cambio en el gateway debe revisarse junto con cualquier cambio en la autorización de middleware.

¿Qué aporta Shirudo?

Shirudo puede cargar protecciones eBPF específicas en un sistema Linux en ejecución sin reiniciarlo para aplicar el escudo. OpenAI describe un flujo de trabajo asistido por agentes para preparar y comprobar un escudo candidato, con operadores que controlan el despliegue. El proyecto describe cargadores firmados para protecciones BPF, verificación del kernel y evidencia respaldada por TPM de los cambios en las protecciones cargadas. Repositorio de Shirudo

El repositorio indica que el proyecto está en fase de prelanzamiento. Enumera un kernel Linux con la ABI de cargador firmado y los parches de kernel de Shirudo, además de TPM 2.0, para entornos de producción. OpenAI plantea la identificación en toda la organización y el despliegue a escala como un objetivo a largo plazo. Presupuesta por separado la preparación de los hosts y la revisión de un cambio temporal. Descripción de OpenAI de la hoja de ruta de Shirudo…

item.title: It's 2 a.m. and the ONTAP Volume Is Offline: A Triage Runbook for the NetApp Certified Support Engineer Exam
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Your phone buzzes at 2:07 a.m. The alert says a database team can't write to its NFS share, and the share lives on an ONTAP cluster you have never logged in to. What do you type first?

That question is the whole point of the NetApp Certified Support Engineer exam (NS0-194, NCSE). It doesn't ask whether you can design a storage array. It asks whether you can walk up to a broken one, find the cause and fix it without making things worse. That's why it also makes a good runbook.

This post is that runbook. Each step maps to one of the six official exam domains, and every command is real ONTAP CLI you can run in a lab or a simulator. You get a better on-call routine and a study plan in one read.

What is the NetApp Certified Support Engineer exam?

The NS0-194 exam validates the skills of an engineer who supports NetApp ONTAP systems on site or remotely. According to NetApp's Support Engineer certification page, it tests general troubleshooting and root cause isolation, hardware replacement, documentation, node configuration, and software and firmware upgrades. NetApp recommends six to 12 months of hands-on experience.

The question count, time and passing score come from the NWExam syllabus page. The domains and experience level come from NetApp. Check the current price on Pearson VUE when you book, because published figures differ between sources.

The six domains are ONTAP OS, troubleshooting NetApp hardware and software, NetApp hardware, NetApp cloud data services, data protection, and Active IQ. The runbook below covers them in the order you'd meet them during a real incident.

Step 1: Is the cluster itself healthy?

Before you look at the volume, look at the ground it stands on. Many "storage is broken" tickets are really a node down, a failed takeover or a network port that went dark.

cluster1::> cluster show

cluster1::> system health status show

cluster1::> system health alert show

cluster1::> storage failover show

cluster show tells you whether every node is healthy and eligible. storage failover show tells you whether the HA pairs are in a normal state or whether one node has taken over its partner. If a takeover happened at 2:01 a.m., you already have a strong lead.

This is the habit the exam rewards: collect information before you change anything. The troubleshooting domain literally lists "How to collect and analyze information" as its first objective.

Step 2: What do disks, aggregates and volumes say?

Next, go one layer up the stack, from physical disks to the aggregate to the volume.

cluster1::> storage disk show -broken

cluster1::> storage aggregate show -fields state,raidstatus

cluster1::> volume show -state offline

cluster1::> volume show -fields percent-used,available -percent-used >90

A quick refresher on the ONTAP OS domain's "disk or aggregate concepts" and "volume concepts":

- Disks are grouped into RAID groups, and RAID groups make up an aggregate.

- An aggregate is the pool of physical capacity on one node.

- FlexVol volumes are carved out of an aggregate and owned by a storage VM (SVM).

- An aggregate in a degraded RAID state still serves data, but losing another disk could take it down.

If the volume is offline and you know why (for example, someone took it offline for maintenance and forgot), bring it back:

cluster1::> volume online -vserver svm_db -volume vol_db01

If it's online but 100% full, writes fail even though nothing is "down". That's one of the most common causes of a "can't write" ticket. Check whether snapshot reserve or a runaway log file is eating the space before you grow the volume.

Step 3: Can the client actually reach the data LIF?

ONTAP serves data through logical interfaces (LIFs) that sit on physical or virtual ports. After a takeover or a cable problem, a LIF can end up on a port that isn't its home port, or on a port with no link at all.

cluster1::> network port show -link down

cluster1::> network interface show -is-home false

cluster1::> network interface show -vserver svm_db -fields address,home-node,curr-node,status-oper

If the LIFs migrated and the home ports are healthy again, send them back:

cluster1::> network interface revert -vserver svm_db -lif *

This is the "ONTAP networking concepts" objective in practice. Know the difference between a physical port, an interface group, a VLAN and a broadcast domain, and know that a LIF fails over within its failover group.

Step 4: Is the client allowed in?

The network is fine and the volume is online, but the client still gets "permission denied". Now you're in the "How to troubleshoot data access problems" objective, which comes up a lot.

For NFS, ONTAP has a built-in command that evaluates the export policy for you. You give it the client IP, protocol and access type, and it shows you which rule matched at every level of the path:

cluster1::> vserver export-policy check-access -vserver svm_db -volume vol_db01 -client-ip 10.20.30.41 -authentication-method sys -protocol nfs3 -access-type read-write

If the result says read where you expected read-write, or denied, look at the rule index it names:

cluster1::> vserver export-policy rule show -vserver svm_db -policyname db_hosts

Common causes are a client match that names the wrong subnet, rw set to never, or a parent junction with a stricter policy than the volume. The check-access output shows each path component, so a parent problem stands out.

For SMB, name resolution and domain connectivity cause most failures:

cluster1::> vserver services name-service dns check -vserver svm_files

cluster1::> vserver cifs show -vserver svm_files

The exam's "Supported ONTAP protocols" and "How ONTAP interacts with external components" objectives cover this: DNS, LDAP, Active Directory, NTP and the clients themselves.

Step 5: Is it slow rather than broken?

Sometimes the ticket says "down" when the truth is "so slow the app timed out". ONTAP can break a volume's latency down by where the time is spent:…

item.title: Virtual Patching vs Patching: Kapan Melindungi API Tanpa Redeploy
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Patching Virtual vs Patching Biasa untuk API: Kapan, Di Mana, dan Kapan Dihapus

Patching virtual untuk sementara memblokir jalur yang diketahui menuju celah perangkat lunak saat kode rentan masih berada di tempatnya. Gunakan saat Anda dapat menjangkau lalu lintas API yang terdampak lebih cepat daripada Anda dapat men-deploy perbaikan dengan aman. Patch dan verifikasi fleet yang terdampak begitu build perbaikan siap.

Pada 23 November 2026, OpenAI dan Cisco memperkenalkan Shirudo, proyek Linux open-source yang dapat memuat proteksi eBPF yang ditargetkan pada sistem yang sedang berjalan. Proyek ini menyoroti keputusan on-call yang sudah lazim. Jika perbaikan permanen membutuhkan waktu berjam-jam untuk divalidasi, dapatkah Anda mengurangi eksposur sekarang tanpa merusak permintaan yang diandalkan pelanggan? Pengumuman Shirudo dari OpenAI

Patching virtual vs patching biasa

Patch virtual adalah kontrol kompensasi. Inventaris Anda masih menampilkan versi rentan selama kontrol aktif. Biarkan tiket remediasi tetap terbuka dan catat aturan, pemilik, serta tanggal penghapusan yang diperkirakan di sana. Panduan patching virtual dari OWASP

Patch biasa dapat berupa library yang diperbarui dalam image container atau build layanan Anda sendiri yang telah diperbaiki. Lacak apa yang benar-benar dijalankan fleet. Image yang telah diperbaiki di registry tidak banyak menjelaskan tentang worker lama yang masih melayani permintaan. Panduan manajemen patch enterprise dari NIST

Kapan Anda perlu melindungi API?

Gunakan perisai saat tiga kondisi berikut terpenuhi.

- Kontrol mencakup lalu lintas yang terdampak. Pastikan jalur ingress dan workload mana yang termasuk dalam cakupan, termasuk pemanggil internal dan pemrosesan latar belakang bila relevan.

- Anda dapat memvalidasinya lebih cepat daripada build perbaikan. Gunakan lalu lintas staging yang representatif untuk memeriksa perilaku aturan yang dimaksud dan memastikan permintaan normal tetap berfungsi.

- Ada yang bertanggung jawab atas jalan keluarnya. Tetapkan rollout patch, sepakati bukti cakupan, dan tentukan waktu tinjauan untuk perubahan sementara.

Misalnya, API objects memiliki fitur pemrosesan opsional yang rentan, dan gateway sudah mendukung penonaktifan akses ke fitur tersebut. Tim Anda dapat menilai perilaku saat dinonaktifkan dengan cepat sambil membangun ulang dan menguji layanan. Pembacaan collection dan detail harus tetap berfungsi. Jika pelanggan menggunakan fitur opsional tersebut, beri tahu tim support respons apa yang akan diterima klien tersebut dan berapa lama perubahan ini kemungkinan berlangsung.

Ukur kedua sisi trade-off. Bandingkan perkiraan waktu untuk menegakkan aturan dengan waktu untuk mendapatkan build perbaikan ke kumpulan workload yang sama. Pantau keberhasilan permintaan normal, latensi, dan jumlah penolakan selama rollout. Kenaikan penolakan perlu konteks. Bisa jadi itu kontrol yang menjalankan tugasnya, atau alur kerja pelanggan yang terlewat oleh fixture staging Anda.

Utamakan patch langsung saat build perbaikan sudah siap, canary terlihat sehat, dan rollout menjangkau instance yang terekspos secepat aturan sementara. Jika tidak ada kontrol tepercaya yang mencakup jalur terdampak dan risiko menuntut tindakan segera, pertimbangkan membatasi akses atau menonaktifkan kemampuan yang terdampak selama perbaikan disiapkan. Jika Anda memiliki bukti kompromi, mulai respons insiden bersamaan dengan remediasi.

Di mana sebaiknya perisai API dijalankan?

Pilih titik penegakan berdasarkan apa yang dapat diamati dan permintaan mana yang harus melewatinya. Web application firewall (WAF) di gateway API mengevaluasi lalu lintas HTTP di sana. Perisai runtime Linux menerapkan kebijakan di tempat host dapat mengamati aktivitas yang relevan. Masing-masing bergantung pada cakupan di lapisannya sendiri.

Aturan gateway cocok untuk perubahan yang menghadap HTTP ketika gateway melihat atribut permintaan yang relevan dan setiap permintaan yang terdampak melewatinya. Verifikasi cakupan terhadap inventaris layanan Anda. Jika suatu layanan menangani pekerjaan dari berbagai sumber, sertakan jalur tersebut dalam rencana remediasi Anda. Untuk contoh spesifik dependensi tentang mengapa inventaris komponen penting, lihat liputan kami tentang kerentanan Node.js Brotli.

Kontrol host masuk akal ketika perilaku yang relevan terlihat di host dan Anda dapat menetapkan cakupan di seluruh kernel dan workload yang terdampak. Penempatannya dapat membawa kontrol lebih dekat ke komponen yang Anda lindungi, dengan persyaratan rollout dan rollback tersendiri. Pertahankan pemeriksaan otorisasi aplikasi dalam rencana pengujian rilis. Perubahan gateway harus berada dalam tinjauan yang sama dengan perubahan apa pun pada otorisasi middleware.

Apa yang ditambahkan Shirudo?

Shirudo dapat memuat proteksi eBPF yang ditargetkan pada sistem Linux yang sedang berjalan tanpa memulai ulang sistem untuk menerapkan perisai. OpenAI menjelaskan alur kerja berbantuan agen untuk menyiapkan dan memeriksa calon perisai, dengan operator yang mengendalikan deployment. Proyek ini menjelaskan loader bertanda tangan untuk proteksi BPF, verifikasi kernel, dan bukti yang didukung TPM atas perubahan pada proteksi yang dimuat. Repositori Shirudo

Repositori tersebut menyebut proyek ini sebagai pra-rilis. Proyek ini mencantumkan kernel Linux dengan ABI signed-loader dan patch kernel Shirudo, ditambah TPM 2.0, untuk target produksi. OpenAI menggambarkan identifikasi dan deployment berskala besar di seluruh organisasi sebagai tujuan jangka panjang. Anggarkan secara terpisah untuk menyiapkan host dan meninjau perubahan sementara. Penjelasan OpenAI tentang peta jalan Shirudo…

item.title: Honor teams up with cinema camera-maker Arri on the Magic 9 Pro Max
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Honor teams up with cinema camera-maker Arri on the Magic 9 Pro Max

Once again, Honor wants to burnish its Hollywood bona fides.

If there's one thing to expect from the launch of a new Honor phone, it's an attempt to burnish its Hollywood bona fides. The advent of the new Magic 9 Pro Max is a chance for the Chinese giant to, as usual, tell the world about how it's once again redefined mobile cinematography. It's the first proper Honor flagship — and second only to the Robot Phone — to benefit from its partnership with Arri. If you're unfamiliar, the German giant makes the Alexa cinema camera, which has shot at least six films which went on to win an Academy Award for cinematography. If nothing else, if your Instagram reel doesn't at least garner a nomination, you know it's not the hardware's fault.

The Magic 9 Pro Max is the first Honor flagship to use the company's new industrial design first seen on its lower-end N series models. That includes a new camera plateau, albeit with a new color contrast back panel around the frame which puts me in mind of... something. Similarly, this is the first Honor flagship to get the Pro Max moniker, a suffix I don't think I've seen elsewhere in the rest of the mobile industry, but which sounds so cool that you think it might inspire copycats.

Nestled inside, you'll find a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 system-on-chip with either 12GB or 16GB RAM and the choice of 256GB, 512GB or 1TB storage. Up front, it's packing a 6.8-inch, 2,868 x 1,320 LTPO OLED display with a 1-120Hz refresh rate and 10,000 nits peak brightness. That's paired with an 8,000mAh battery which can support up to 100W wired or 80W wireless charging. Rounding out the useful specs are Wi-Fi 7, space for two SIM cards as well as an eSIM and a 55-megapixel front-facing camera.

Of course, these are all just supporting players for the main event, the Arriflex-inspired triple camera system 'round back. It's equipped with a 200-megapixel, f/1.57 OIS primary lens and a 200-megapixel f/2.6 OIS telephoto, as well as a 50-megapixel f/2.0 ultra-wide camera. Of note is that Honor claims the primary lens has "gimbal" levels of optical stabilization to keep your shots as smooth as possible, no matter how you old it.

To make use of all those megapixels, Honor is launching its first dedicated imaging processor, the H1, and grabbed plenty of Arri's know-how. Honor says the Magic 9 Pro Max uses an end-to-end cinematic workflow, shooting high-end video in Arri LogC3 — the company's version of Log — as well as a series of Arri-created filters and color profiles you can apply to your footage. You'll have a pick of up to 87 Arri looks to apply to your footage, and you can even shoot in Cinema ratios like 2.39:1.

To further bolster its credentials in this arena, Honor is launching a series of accessories in partnership with SmallRig. Equip your phone with the SmallRig camera cage and you'll be able to attach it to either the Honor-branded Teleconverter G200 or the Teleconverter G500. They'll increase the phone's focal length by either 200mm or 500mm, enabling you to shoot distances you'd struggle to capture with AI-enhanced imaging.

Honor's Magic 9 Pro Max is debuting in Malaysia, priced at RM 5,999 (approx $1,455) for the 12GB RAM / 512GB storage option. It'll arrive in the Middle East next month, and take its first bow in the West at some point in January.

Source: Engadget | Published: 2026-11-24 09:00 UTC

item.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

At QCon San Francisco 2026, Brian Yang, Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI, described how a small group of engineers used coding agents to build the ChatGPT ads product, reaching $100 million in annualised recurring revenue within six weeks of launch and $1 billion in under 200 days, with zero human-written code.

Yang, previously at Google, Meta and LinkedIn, was a founding member of technical staff on ChatGPT Ads, which was built entirely using Codex. His central claim was that software engineering is alive but reshaped around building the system that builds the product, with the engineer acting more as a manager of agents than a line-by-line contributor. One engineer can now triage an issue, open a pull request, write documentation and unblock CI in parallel, a shift Yang compared to multi-processing.

Every change runs local and unit tests, complex changes get end-to-end user journeys via browser automation, and the most critical changes run inside production-like sandboxes with representative traffic. Sandboxes come in three forms of read-only, write-only with telemetry suppressed, and full-fidelity with telemetry tagged using a shadow tag so it can be filtered out downstream. Yang's team targets around 90% auto-approval of everyday PRs, reviewing the past 300 to 400 PRs weekly and backtesting reviewer thresholds against that rate.

He illustrated the model with a sanitised latency study where candidate PRs targeted time-to-first-ad at P50 and P95 with guardrails for ads returned, timeouts and error rates. Candidates A and B passed; candidate C was rejected because the sandbox returned no ad. Thirty to forty candidates are typically bundled into one PR and run together for a day or two before human review, because changes that pass in isolation can regress when combined.

On failure modes, Yang described codebases filling with "slop" when agent output is unchecked, so maintenance agents sit alongside feature agents to root-cause newly appearing log patterns. Agents over-write tests, so he reviews the 50 slowest tests weekly. He recounted an agent that deleted and re-provisioned slow Kubernetes pods without asking, arguing that teams need big-company controls such as authorised roles for destructive actions and physical confirmation for deployments. Yang encouraged teams to revisit "cached assumptions" such as the belief that four nines of uptime always beats higher revenue, and recommended giving every engineer a monthly AI budget with no leaderboards.

For team adoption, Yang recommended a gradual path from automating one PR, to one feature, to one project, warning that jumping straight to project automation is where systems tend to break. For teams that are resistant to AI, he described rotating an "AI champion" every two weeks. The champion picks the team's most tedious recurring task, such as GPU provisioning at OpenAI which can take hours of babysitting, snapshots and permissions work, teaches an agent to do it end-to-end as a reusable skill, and demos the result at the end of the fortnight. Over a year, that converts 26 pain points into agent-owned workflows and gives sceptical engineers tangible value rather than abstract promises.

Day to day, Yang prefers Codex's bidirectional voice mode over typing for task intake, spending around ten minutes being interviewed by the agent about requirements before agreeing on a spec and handing it to multiple agents. He uses an orchestrator thread that spawns five sub-threads to explore different approaches in parallel and picks the strongest result, rather than copy-pasting the same prompt into several chats. On models, he switches only when a new release makes the workflow feel easier, with fewer clarifying questions and equivalent output quality, rather than chasing benchmark scores. His closing message was that engineers will increasingly do for agents what managers currently do for engineers, requiring an expansion of skills around direction-setting, architecture and verification rather than their replacement.

Source: InfoQ | Published: 2026-11-24 06:32 UTC

item.title: 2035 Came Early
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

tl;dr trynix.dev boots GUI programs now. Try solitaire, GL gears, xeyes, a voice, the weather over curl, or Firefox.

I remember watching the talk The Birth & Death of JavaScript by Gary Bernhardt and falling in love with the whimsical yet dreadfully serious unfolding of the story of how JavaScript will come to dominate all software.

Others have noted the inevitability of JavaScript’s dominance, so perhaps it was not surprising that Atwood’s Law holds true.

Atwood’s LawAny application that can be written in JavaScript, will eventually be written in JavaScript. — Jeff Atwood, 2009

I highly recommend watching the talk if you have not already seen it, but the short and skinny is a lookback from 2035 and how JavaScript came to be the defacto language for all software.

In Bernhardt’s retelling of events, the date is worked back from 2035, however unsurprisingly, large language models have rapidly sped up the timeline. What was once perceived to be the end-state at 2035 has arrived years earlier and you can witness it unfolding at trynix.dev.

One of the most impressive creations I’ve managed to build leveraging nixpkgs-multiverse is https://trynix.dev.

It still baffles my mind that I can run any Nix package, over 300,000 distinct package versions, straight from my browser. Truly insane capability. I was however a little dismayed at the speed of the QEMU emulation in the browser. It was slow enough that the creation tipped more towards novelty than practicality.

I woke on November 20th and saw Domen Kožar sharing a single message in our TacoSprint Discord channel: unkernel.dev

It was the fast browser Linux experience I had sought to achieve, but with Nix.

Aside What is unkernel? It is Linux compiled to WebAssembly, allowing the kernel and system components to run at wasm speed while only user programs are emulated. It was published by Pooya Parsa on November 19th, 2026.

In an AI induced manic frenzy, I adopted the new engine along with a slough of long-wished features almost immediately.

The proof is in the pudding: unkernel delivers remarkable speed improvements over qemu-wasm,11With a very healthy set of patches applied to make it even faster. especially on first runs where kernel work dominates. The new engine is able to deliver 2x to 32x faster performance depending on the workload.22The benchmark page tracks both engines over time, measured through the real page and shell.

JavaScript & WebAssembly nirvana.

Amazingly not only does the kernel boot quickly, it also enables networking, full-fledged graphical and audio experiences directly in the browser.

Windows. A program’s Wayland surfaces are composited in the page by wland, and they float over the terminal you started them from.

GL. The VM includes a minimal Mesa build with only the virgl driver, compiled to WebAssembly, rendering through your browser’s WebGL2.

Sound. The VM has an ALSA sound card, and can play audio through your browser.

Network. curl, git clone and pip install work. Each TCP connection goes over one WebSocket to a Wisp relay.33Thank you to @_pi0_ for adding trynix.dev to his Wisp relay allow-list.

The best joke in Bernhardt’s talk is a browser running inside another browser: the Windows GIMP under Wine, in Chrome, in Firefox. Of course, I had to try it with trynix. 😈

Here is Firefox in trynix, and it loading trynix.dev, and then loading Firefox again inside itself.44Do not be too overjoyed. It took more than an hour for this to render.

Sit and bask in that insanity. That is Firefox, on Linux compiled to WebAssembly, in a Firefox tab, loading the site and then loading Firefox again inside itself. 🤯

2035 came early.

item.title: Apple confirms Ted Lasso will return for Season 5
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Apple confirms Ted Lasso will return for Season 5

The mustachioed coach will be back on the pitch dealing out folksy advice once again.

Ted Lasso, which everyone thought was ending with season three, has just been renewed for a fifth season. "Following its hit fourth season, Apple's global phenomenon Ted Lasso is officially returning back to the pitch for season five," Apple said in a press release, though it revealed no details about the show's next iteration.

The show wrapped up its storyline about the men's AFC Richmond Premier League squad (aka the Greyhounds) at the end of season three. Following the final episode of that season, called "So Long, Farewell," co-creator and lead actor Jason Sudeikis said "this is the end of the story we wanted to tell."

Thanks for believing.#TedLasso has been renewed for Season 5. pic.twitter.com/epfW8riG7b

— Apple TV (@AppleTV) November 23, 2026

Sounds pretty definitive! But then, the showrunners came up with the inspired idea for a fourth season: switching from the men's team to the Division 2 Lady Greyhounds. Though not quite hitting the critical heights of seasons one and two, it outperformed the Lasso's third run with an excellent 90 percent Rotten Tomatoes critical rating.

Season four ended with the Lady Greyhounds promoted to the women's Super League, ownership of the team settled and nice storyline wrap-ups for some of the main characters including Roy Kent, Keely, Coaches Lasso and Beard, Rebecca, and Alice Chilton. However, Apple didn't say if the show would stick with the Lady Greyhounds or shift its story elsewhere.

Love it or hate it, Ted Lasso is more than just a successful show for Apple TV. It was the platform's first bonafide hit, helping set a marker for future popular series like Severance, Silo, The Studio, Pluribus and Widow's Bay.
